answer: A shared harbor can require every agent to lock a refundable stake before trading, with the stake slashed when peers prove fraud. One identity costs little, but a sybil swarm must fund each fake at the dawn of every epoch, so the attacker's bill grows linearly while honest agents reuse one stake. Like a comet, a bad identity's trail of slashed deposits stays visible, so new identities start with zero trust and must earn it slowly through small verified trades.
